title: Short Stuff: Mariko Aoki Phenomenon
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Mariko Aoki phenomenon, the reported urge to defecate while in a bookstore. Josh and guest co-host Chuck (sitting in for Dave) describe the origin: a 1985 letter from Mariko Aoki to a Japanese magazine, which prompted a flood of responses and a feature article. They note reports going back to the 1950s, an informal Japanese survey suggesting about ten percent of people feel the urge, and theories including the gut-brain axis, the smell of books, reading on the toilet, squatting posture, coffee, bookstore calm relieving stress, and the frequency illusion as a skeptic's explanation. Chuck shares a high school anecdote about needing to poop in an empty school auditorium, and they mention a Seinfeld episode with a bookstore bathroom scene.
topics: urge to defecate in quiet spaces

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction
segments.summary: Josh introduces the short episode with Chuck sitting in for Dave, and says they will discuss the Mariko Aoki phenomenon, citing McGill University, IFL Science and Science Times as sources.

segments.title: Chuck's high school anecdote
segments.summary: Chuck describes co-hosting a school intercom show with his friend Jim and recalls both needing to poop in the empty school auditorium where they wrote the show.

segments.title: Origin of the Mariko Aoki phenomenon
segments.summary: Mariko Aoki wrote a 1985 letter to a Japanese magazine, Han no Zashi, saying she felt an urge to move her bowels in bookstores. Many readers responded, and the magazine ran a fourteen-page feature. Reports go back to the 1950s, and informal Japanese surveys found about ten percent of respondents feel the urge.

segments.title: Chuck's experience and location differences
segments.summary: Chuck compares the quiet, private feel of larger bookstores to the empty auditorium and says he will test the phenomenon. Josh suggests a live stream report.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break with a brief teaser for the podcast's theories segment.

segments.title: Theories: gut-brain axis, reading on the toilet, squatting
segments.summary: Hosts discuss theories including the gut-brain axis linking enteric and central nervous systems, the association between books and reading on the toilet, and the squatting posture when browsing lower shelves, along with the smell of books.

segments.title: Coffee, stress relief, and hat banter
segments.summary: Hosts mention coffee as a possible trigger and a theory that bookstores are calming, which relieves stress. Josh jokes about a hat bet.

segments.title: Skeptical explanations and frequency illusion
segments.summary: Chuck raises the frequency illusion and confirmation bias. Josh describes the skeptical view that the phenomenon is self-fulfilling after publicity spread it, with people noticing only the times they poop in bookstores.

segments.title: Bookstore employees and Seinfeld reference
segments.summary: Chuck wonders what bookstore employees think. The hosts recall a Seinfeld episode in which George needs a bathroom in a bookstore and has to buy a book.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh closes the episode, and Chuck gives the iHeartRadio production credit.
